articles.description:
Three AI moves hitting your bank, your government's security table, and your anime queue:
① ChatGPT's Personal Finance feature opens to all Plus subscribers
Before you link: check the privacy settings. Connecting a bank account to any AI is a real security decision, not a convenience upgrade.
② OpenAI built GPT-5.6 Sol, Terra, and Luna — the White House said "not yet"
We've seen this before: Anthropic's Fable 5 was blocked in June, then Mythos 5 got a partial lift days later. OpenAI themselves said "we don't believe this should become the long-term default." Pricing is already public (Luna: $1/M tokens, Sol: $5/M). GA expected within weeks.
③ Japan's government is paying $70M to speed up anime subtitles with AI
Japan's METI is putting up $70M USD (¥11.5B) to cover 50% of AI translation and localization costs. Partners include Crunchyroll, Shueisha, Bandai Namco, Kodansha, and Square Enix. Goal: grow the official global subscriber base from 100M to 300M. Modeled on South Korea's KOCCA strategy — which worked.
The pattern: AI tools are crossing from research labs into your bank, your government's security clearance table, and your anime queue — all at the same time.
🎙 Narration by Charlotte (ElevenLabs)
articles.title: ChatGPT Just Read My Bank Statement, GPT-5.6 Got White-Housed, and Japan Dropped $70M on Anime Subs — AI News Jun 28

articles.author: simbamkenya
articles.description:
Like many developers, I was frustrated by searching for AI engineering jobs across dozens of company career pages.
Most job boards are either:
Too broad.
Full of duplicate listings.
Slow to remove closed jobs.
Or label old jobs as "new."
So I decided to build AIRAG Jobs.
The idea is simple: aggregate AI engineering jobs directly from company career pages and enrich them with AI-powered metadata.
Today, AIRAG Jobs tracks 420+ verified jobs from 20 AI companies, focused on:
LLM Engineering
Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)
AI Agents
ML Infrastructure
AI Platform Engineering
Every job is scraped directly from the employer's careers page and regularly checked so closed positions disappear automatically.
Laravel
Sveltkit
Mysql
AI-powered job enrichment
Scheduled scrapers
Queue workers for processing jobs
Each job is enriched with structured information such as skills, technologies, seniority, and role categories to make searching much easier.
One interesting lesson came this week.
I thought my scraper had failed because there were zero new jobs in the last 24 hours.
After checking every company, I realized nothing was broken—there simply weren't any new AI engineering jobs posted.
I'd rather show 0 genuinely new jobs than make old listings look fresh.
I'm expanding from 20 companies to hundreds while keeping the quality high. The goal isn't to build the biggest AI job board—it's to build one developers can trust.
If you're an AI engineer looking for your next role, or you're building something similar, I'd love to hear your thoughts.
AIRAG Jobs: https://airagjobs.com/
articles.title: # Building AIRAG Jobs: A Job Board for LLM, RAG & AI Agent Engineers

articles.author: David Harvey
articles.description:
If you send SMS one-time codes, there's a decent chance you're paying scammers to phone-spam themselves on your dime. It even has a name: SMS pumping. And it's not a rounding error — Elon Musk claimed Twitter was losing ~$60M/year to fake 2FA traffic before they killed SMS 2FA for free accounts.
Here's how the scam works, why SMS 2FA is structurally expensive, and why flipping the direction — mobile-originated (MO) 2FA, taken to its logical end over iMessage — fixes both the cost and the fraud at once.
SMS pumping (also called AIT — Artificially Inflated Traffic, or SMS toll fraud) is a scheme where bad actors abuse a form that sends SMS one-time codes. They pump thousands of phone numbers — usually premium ranges they secretly control with a telecom — into your "send me a code" endpoint.
…
articles.title: SMS Pumping Is Draining Your 2FA Budget — and Mobile-Originated iMessage 2FA Fixes It

articles.author: gpszxtzys
articles.description:
I spent last month migrating 23 client sites from JPEG/PNG to WebP and AVIF. Here's what I wish someone told me before I started.
AVIF is about 30% smaller than WebP at the same quality level. But Safari support is still patchy — if your traffic is 40%+ iOS, you need <picture> tags with WebP fallback. No way around it.
The single biggest reduction came from capping max image width at 1200px and setting quality to 80. One site went from 9.4MB to 318KB per page — a 97% reduction — just from those two settings plus lazy loading.
The format switch was the cherry on top, not the cake.
SmartImgKit — quick batch conversions in the browser. No uploads, no signup, drag and drop. Handles the 80% case where you don't need a CLI pipeline. Supports JPG, PNG, WebP, AVIF, GIF, BMP, TIFF.
ImageMagick — server-side batch jobs for when you need automation.
Squoosh — one-off fine-tuning with visual comparison.
Sharp (Node.js) — build pipeline integration.
Every iPhone user's photos are HEIC. Most web tools crash on them. You need a converter that handles them before the pipeline — SmartImgKit's HEIC converter works locally in-browser, no uploads.
Format + max width + lazy loading = 80% of the gain. Everything else is diminishing returns. Don't over-engineer it.
articles.title: I switched 23 sites from JPEG to WebP/AVIF last month — here's what I learned
